title: Practice Exam 5
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: What does it mean when a bicyclist extends their left arm down with the palm facing back?
choices: The cyclist intends to stop or slow down
The cyclist intends to turn left
The cyclist intends to turn right
The cyclist is signaling you to pass
questions.explanation: A left arm pointed downward signals that the bicyclist is stopping or slowing down.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: What is the maximum speed allowed when crossing railroad tracks within 100 feet where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in both directions?
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
10 mph
20 mph
questions.explanation: You may not drive faster than 15 mph within 100 feet of a railroad crossing where you cannot see the tracks for 400 feet in each direction.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: Why must you not follow too closely behind a responding fire engine or ambulance?
choices: It may stop suddenly, and you could interfere with emergency operations
Emergency vehicles drive much slower than traffic
It is legal as long as you stay in the same lane
Following closely helps clear traffic faster
questions.explanation: Responding emergency vehicles may stop or maneuver suddenly, so staying at least 300 feet back keeps you safe and out of their way.

questions.question: If you find another vehicle to your side blocking your space cushion, what should you do?
choices: Change your speed to open a gap so you have an escape route
Maintain the same speed and stay alongside them
Speed up only and never slow down
Move into their lane to claim the space
questions.explanation: Avoid driving in another vehicle's blind spot or alongside it; adjust your speed to keep open space and an escape path around you.

questions.question: Which of the following is an illegal place to park or leave your vehicle?
choices: On a sidewalk or blocking a driveway
On the shoulder of a rural road outside city limits
In a marked parking stall at a shopping center
On a residential street with no posted restrictions
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park on a sidewalk, in a crosswalk, or blocking a driveway, among other restricted locations.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking (Where It Is Illegal to Park)

questions.question: What does a yellow diamond sign with a symbol of a car and wavy lines beneath it warn of?
choices: The road may be slippery when wet
A car wash is located ahead
Flooding has closed the road
A boat launch or ferry is ahead
questions.explanation: The slippery-road warning sign (a car with skid marks/wavy lines) means the surface can be slick, especially when wet, so slow down and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: A pedestrian steps into an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection without traffic signals. What must you do?
choices: Yield the right of way to the pedestrian
Proceed because only marked crosswalks require yielding
Continue, since the pedestrian must wait for traffic to clear
Sound your horn and maintain your speed
questions.explanation: Crosswalks exist at intersections even when not marked with painted lines, and you must yield to pedestrians crossing in them.

questions.question: You should program your GPS or select your music playlist:
choices: Before you begin driving
While stopped at red lights along the way
Slowly while driving so it takes less attention
Whenever traffic is light
questions.explanation: Set up navigation and audio before you start driving, or have a passenger handle it, so you keep your attention on the road.

questions.question: When a railroad-crossing signal's red lights are flashing, what must you do?
choices: Stop and wait; do not cross until the lights stop flashing and any gates are fully raised
Cross quickly before the train arrives
Slow down but continue if no train is visible
Stop only if a gate is lowered
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean stop and stay stopped until the lights stop and gates rise; never drive around lowered gates.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a manual distraction while driving?
choices: Eating or reaching for a snack
Daydreaming about your plans
Listening to a passenger talk
Thinking about a stressful phone call
questions.explanation: Manual distractions take your hands off the wheel, such as eating, drinking, or reaching for an object. Daydreaming and worrying are cognitive distractions.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road, with a broken yellow line on the other side, means what for you?
choices: You may not pass; the broken line side may pass
You may pass whenever you wish
Both directions may pass freely
Neither direction may pass
questions.explanation: When the line on your side is solid, you may not cross it to pass, while traffic on the side with the broken line is allowed to pass.

questions.question: On a one-way street with three lanes, when can you change lanes?
choices: You may move between any lanes when it is safe and you have signaled
You may only move toward the right
Lane changes are never allowed on one-way streets
You may only move toward the left curb lane
questions.explanation: On a one-way street, traffic moves in a single direction, so you may change between any lanes as long as you signal and the move is safe.

questions.question: You must never park or stop your vehicle where with respect to a fire station?
choices: Within 20 feet of a fire station driveway, or directly across the street within 75 feet of a posted fire station entrance
Within 5 feet of a fire station on the same side only
Anywhere on the same block as a fire station
Within 100 feet of a fire station in any direction
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway, or on the opposite side of the street within 75 feet of a posted fire station entrance.

questions.question: What are the three main types of driver distraction?
choices: Visual, manual, and cognitive
Loud, quiet, and sudden
Mechanical, electrical, and chemical
Front, side, and rear
questions.explanation: Distractions are visual (eyes off the road), manual (hands off the wheel), and cognitive (mind off driving). Texting involves all three at once.

questions.question: Some posted speed limits near senior centers or recreation areas are reduced because:
choices: Slower-moving or less aware pedestrians may be crossing
The road surface is rougher there
Those roads are wider
Fewer cars drive there
questions.explanation: Reduced speed limits near senior centers, parks, and similar areas protect pedestrians who may move slowly or be less aware of traffic.

questions.question: Driving while impaired by an illegal drug, prescription medication, or marijuana is treated under California law as:
choices: A DUI, the same as driving impaired by alcohol
A minor traffic infraction only
Legal as long as no alcohol is involved
Allowed if the drug was prescribed by a doctor
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug, whether illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter. Drugged driving is charged as a DUI.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: You want to make a left turn at an intersection with a green light (no green arrow) and oncoming traffic is approaching. What should you do?
choices: Yield to oncoming traffic and turn only when there is a safe gap
Turn immediately because you arrived at the intersection first
Make the turn since oncoming traffic must yield to left-turning cars
Proceed because a green light gives left turns priority
questions.explanation: On a solid green light, left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: A school bus stopped on a two-lane undivided road has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended. Drivers approaching from the opposite direction must:
choices: Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop and the arm retracts
Slow to 25 mph and pass
Continue if no children are crossing
Pass on the left side
questions.explanation: On an undivided road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus with red flashing lights and an extended stop arm until it withdraws the signals.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road / School Buses

questions.question: You are leaving a parking lot and crossing a sidewalk to enter the street. Who has the right of way?
choices: Pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles on the street
You, because you are already moving
Only pedestrians, not the vehicles on the street
No one; first to move proceeds
questions.explanation: When crossing a sidewalk and entering a roadway from a parking lot or driveway, you must yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk and to vehicles on the street.

questions.question: What do flashing YELLOW lights on a school bus mean?
choices: The bus is preparing to stop, so slow down and be ready
You must stop immediately from both directions
The bus is broken down
Children are already crossing
questions.explanation: Flashing yellow lights warn that the bus is about to stop to load or unload children; slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road / School Buses

questions.question: What does a yellow diamond sign with two curving arrows pointing in opposite directions (an S-shape) warn of?
choices: A winding road with several curves ahead
A divided highway begins
A roundabout is ahead
Two-way traffic resumes
questions.explanation: The double-curve/winding-road symbol warns that the road ahead curves in more than one direction, so reduce speed. A single curved arrow would mean just one curve.

questions.question: What does a yellow pennant-shaped (sideways triangle) sign on the left side of a two-lane road indicate?
choices: The beginning of a no-passing zone
A yield to oncoming traffic
The end of a divided highway
A pedestrian crosswalk ahead
questions.explanation: The yellow pennant 'No Passing Zone' sign is posted on the left and marks where passing is prohibited. It works together with the solid yellow centerline.

questions.question: What does a green painted curb indicate?
choices: Parking is allowed for a limited time only
Parking is allowed for disabled placard holders only
Loading zone for freight or commercial vehicles
No parking at any time
questions.explanation: A green curb means parking is permitted for a limited time, posted on a nearby sign or painted on the curb.

questions.question: When may a bicyclist legally ride in the center of the traffic lane?
choices: When the lane is too narrow to share safely with a vehicle
Never, bicyclists must always stay at the curb
Only on freeways
Only when no cars are present
questions.explanation: Bicyclists may use the full lane when it is too narrow to share safely, when avoiding hazards, or when preparing to turn left.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: Motorcycles in California are legally allowed to do which of the following between lanes of slow or stopped traffic?
choices: Lane split, meaning ride between rows of vehicles
Drive on the freeway shoulder to pass
Make U-turns across double yellow lines anywhere
Ride two motorcycles side by side in one car's blind spot
questions.explanation: Lane splitting, riding a motorcycle between rows of stopped or slow-moving vehicles, is legal in California. Drivers should be aware and not block motorcyclists.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Motorcycles

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic signal require you to do?
choices: Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe, as you would at a stop sign
Slow down and proceed without stopping
Stop and wait for the light to turn green
Treat it as a yield sign and merge
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal means the same as a stop sign: come to a full stop, then go when it is safe. A flashing yellow means slow and proceed with caution.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: When you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane at a corner, you should:
choices: Always yield the right of way
Proceed if you reach the corner first
Wait only if they have started crossing
Honk to alert them of your presence
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane always have the right of way; stop and let them cross safely.

questions.question: If you are driving slower than the flow of traffic on a multi-lane highway, what should you do?
choices: Keep to the right lane so faster traffic can pass on the left
Stay in the left lane to be out of the way
Speed up to match the fastest vehicles regardless of safety
Use your hazard lights and remain in any lane
questions.explanation: Slower traffic must keep right; the left lanes are for passing and faster-moving vehicles. This keeps traffic flowing safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving Too Slowly

questions.question: Following distance is best thought of as a measure of what?
choices: Time, not just space, between you and the vehicle ahead
Only the number of car lengths ahead of you
The speed limit on the road
The width of your lane
questions.explanation: The three-second rule measures following distance in time, which automatically adjusts the gap as your speed changes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Distance (Three-Second Rule)

questions.question: When you are driving on the freeway and another vehicle is trying to merge from an on-ramp, what is the courteous and safe response?
choices: Move over a lane if possible, or adjust speed to let them merge
Speed up to close the gap and prevent them from merging
Stop in your lane to let them in
Move onto the right shoulder to give them your lane
questions.explanation: Help merging traffic by moving over one lane when it is safe, or by adjusting your speed to open a gap, rather than blocking them.

questions.question: When driving near senior centers, parks, or where elderly pedestrians may be present, how should you handle your speed?
choices: Slow down and obey any posted reduced limits because pedestrians may move slowly or unexpectedly
Maintain normal speed since pedestrians must yield
Speed up to clear the area quickly
Speed limits never change for these areas
questions.explanation: Authorities may post reduced limits near senior centers, parks, and similar areas; slow down and watch for pedestrians who may be slow to cross.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: Why is keeping a proper following distance especially important behind a motorcycle?
choices: Motorcycles can stop quickly and you need extra time to react
Motorcycles always travel below the speed limit
Motorcycles are required to brake gradually
Motorcycles take much longer to stop than cars
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop in a short distance, so allow extra following distance (four or more seconds) to give yourself time to react.

questions.question: Using marijuana, even where it is legal, before driving is:
choices: Illegal and chargeable as a DUI if it impairs your driving
Always legal as long as you are over 21
Permitted if a passenger holds the marijuana
Allowed on local streets but not freeways
questions.explanation: Although recreational marijuana is legal for adults in California, driving while impaired by it is a DUI just like alcohol.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: If you are on DUI probation, what is the maximum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) you are allowed to have while driving?
questions.explanation: California's zero-tolerance law sets a 0.01% BAC limit for drivers on DUI probation, regardless of age. Any measurable alcohol can result in penalties.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol, Drugs, and Driving

questions.question: You are parking on a level street that has no curb. What should you do with the front wheels?
choices: Turn them toward the edge of the road or shoulder
Leave them pointed straight ahead
Turn them toward the center of the road
Wheel direction does not matter on a level street
questions.explanation: With no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle would roll away from traffic if it moved.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on a Hill

questions.question: You are approaching a roadway construction zone where a lane is closed ahead. What is the recommended way to merge?
choices: Signal early and merge into the open lane when there is a safe gap
Wait until the lane ends and then force your way in
Stop in the closed lane and wait for someone to wave you in
Straddle both lanes to block others from passing
questions.explanation: In a construction zone with a closing lane, signal early and merge smoothly into the open lane when a safe gap appears, rather than waiting until the last moment.
